messages.content:
You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in an orthorhombic unit cell with lattice parameters a = 5.051578 Å, b = 5.47001 Å, and c = 7.329205 Å, all interaxial angles being exactly 90°. The input composition is Nd₂Mg₂Ni₈H₈, corresponding to 20 atoms per unit cell. The space group is Pmn2₁ (number 31, Hall symbol P 2ac -2), a non-centrosymmetric orthorhombic space group with a mirror plane perpendicular to the a-axis, a glide plane perpendicular to b, and a twofold screw axis along c. The input and standard crystallographic frames coincide exactly: the transformation q_standard = P q_input + s uses the identity matrix P and a zero origin shift s = (0, 0, 0), so the fractional coordinates given below are directly those of the conventional setting. All coordinates were recorded to six decimal places, and no precision corrections were required.

The asymmetric unit contains eight independent atomic orbits. Two distinct metal sites and two hydrogen sites lie on the twofold special position 2a, with coordinates constrained to the form (0, y, z) on the mirror plane at x = 0. Neodymium occupies one such 2a orbit with y = 0.298301 and z = 0.001574, placing the Nd atoms near the ab face of the cell, slightly offset from z = 0. Magnesium occupies a second 2a orbit at y = 0.818261 and z = 0.223345, shifted roughly a quarter of the way up the c-axis. Two independent nickel sublattices also reside on 2a positions: one at y = 0.449059, z = 0.621999, and the other at y = 0.992981, z = 0.604088, the latter lying very close to the b cell edge (y ≈ 1) at a similar height in c. Two further hydrogen orbits complete the 2a set: one at y = 0.721338, z = 0.5115, and another at y = 0.938316, z = 0.824162.

The remaining atoms occupy the general fourfold position 4b with unconstrained coordinates (x, y, z). A third, fourfold nickel orbit is centered at x = 0.244043, y = 0.228688, z = 0.379044; the mirror and glide operations of Pmn2₁ generate the full set of four equivalent Ni atoms from this representative. A fourfold hydrogen orbit sits at x = 0.248446, y = 0.490274, z = 0.257773, at nearly the same x-coordinate as the general nickel site but displaced along b and c.

Taken together, the 2a multiplicities (Nd 2, Mg 2, Ni 2 + 2, H 2 + 2) plus the two 4b orbits (Ni 4, H 4) reproduce the declared cell content of Nd₂Mg₂Ni₈H₈. The three inequivalent nickel sublattices—two on the mirror plane at x = 0 and one in the general position—along with the three inequivalent hydrogen sublattices, define the full three-dimensional arrangement: atoms on the 2a planes at x = 0 and (by symmetry) x = ½ are interleaved with the general-position Ni and H atoms at x ≈ 0.25 and x ≈ 0.75, generating a layered stacking along a with the various species distributed at distinct heights along c.
